intended_object: A smart constructor that packages the label `B 2 q` and a proof that it is valid into an element of the library's subtype `TypeB2LieIndex`. That subtype collects the validated labels for the untwisted family B₂(q) in the CFSG classification list. The reading comes from the docstring and from the companion lemma `exists_eq_of`.
explanation:
The body only bundles data. `RankTwoBLieIndex.ofB q hvalid` gives the validated label whose Dynkin type is B₂. A `simp` proof then shows that this label is not the Suzuki one (`UsesHalfFrobenius`). The result lands in `TypeB2LieIndex := {d : RankTwoBLieIndex // ¬d.1.1.UsesHalfFrobenius}`.

This is bookkeeping for the library's own index types. The definition does not construct the group B₂(q) or any other mathematical object; it only builds an element of a subtype of labels. The construction is also consistent: `exists_eq_of` shows that every element of `TypeB2LieIndex` arises this way. The docstring says validity forces `4 ≤ q.card`; this is the separate lemma `four_le_fieldOrder`, which reflects the B₂(2) duplicate exclusion.

Mathlib has no counterpart for this kind of indexing device. It is an implementation detail, not a mathematical notion that could be judged faithful or not.
